Title:
Standard Test Method for Nitrate Ion in Water.
Procedure:
Introduction

This document outlines the 
 testing procedures P1, which must be performed on a monthly 
 basis as indicated by M1 in the above title block, and according to the 
 Directives of the Central Chemical Laboratories.

This method covers the 
 determination of nitrate ion in water. Samples containing 1 to 50 mg/Liter of 
 nitrate, as NO3, may be analyzed by this method. The concentration 
 range may be extended by dilution of an appropriate aliquot.

This document is Forbbiden at 30 Dec 2008 for 
this reason:

items:
This test its reagent (Brucine) is 
 carcinogenic, and this method doesn't become used at modern ASTM after 
 1981. 
 Note: We Highly Recommended not 
 to use this method but use Ion Chromatograph Method for the 
 determination of 
 Nitrate Ion in Water 
 which will be Wtr-006-r1.

sections.text: Summary of Method

Nitrate ion reacts with brucine in strong 
 sulfuric acid solution to develop a yellow color. The color does not follow 
 the Beer-Lambert relationship. However, a plot of absorbance versus 
 concentration produces a smooth curve. It is necessary to develop a series of 
 standards simultaneously with the samples. The color is measured at 410 nm.

The rate of color development varies directly 
 with the temperature and the intensity varies inversely with the temperature.
Interferences

Strong oxidizing or reducing agents 
interfere. Oxidizing agents may be determined with orthotolidine. Chlorine interference up to 5 mg/liter 
may be eliminated by the addition of sodium arsenite.

High content of organic matter may 
interfere by increasing the absorbance readings at 410 nm and also because of 
the possible charring effects from the concentrated sulfuric acid (H2SO4).This 
can be minimized by pretreatment with aluminum 
hydroxide and specially treated activated carbon.

Nitrite interference up to 7 mg/liter 
is eliminated by the sulfanilic acid in the brucine reagent solution.

Table 1 shows the amount of various 
other substances commonly found in water without causing interference in this test.

TABLE 1 Concentrations of Added 
Substances That Do Not Cause Interference a

a The listed 
concentrations do not represent the maximum amounts of impurities that can be 
present before interference with the nitrate determination is experienced. 
Instead, they indicate an amount of each impurity that has been observed to have 
no effect.

Safety 
Precautions

items:
Cleaning solvents such as acid 
 dichromate, nitric acid and others are 
 dangerous, so 
 you have to wear breathing mask.

Keep 
 this solvents closed. Do not get it in the eyes, on the skin, or on clothing. Do 
 not breathe them, use only in a hood.

sections.text: Tools and Equipment
Apparatus
Photometer

A spectrophotometer or filter photometer suitable 
for measurements at 410 nm with a light path of 1 to 5 cm.
Reagents and Materials
Purity of Reagents

All reagents shall conform to the 
 specifications of the committee on Analytical Reagents of the American 
 Chemical Society, where such specifications are available. Other grades may be 
 used, provided that the reagent is of high purity to permit its use without 
 lessening the accuracy of the determination.
Purity of Water

Unless otherwise indicated, 
 references to water shall be understood to mean reagent water conforming to 
 Type 1 of ASTM Specification D 1193, for reagent water.
Activated Carbon

Heat fine grain (0.2 to 0.5-mm 
 diameter ) activated carbon to red heat in an atmosphere of carbon dioxide , 
 cool, extract with n-hexane, and wash with water at 80C.
Aluminum Hydroxide Cream

Dissolve 124 g of potassium or 
 ammonium alum in 1 liter of water. Heat to 50C and slowly add with stirring 
 55 ml of ammonium hydroxide ( NH4OH, sp gr 0.90 ). Let stand 1h, and then wash 
 the precipitate with water by mixing and decanting until free from ammonia 
 chloride, nitrate, and nitrite ions.

Brucine - Sulfanilic Acid 
 Solution

Dissolve 1 g of brucine sulfate (
 Caution: Note1 ) and 0.1 g of sulfanilic acid in approximately 70 ml of 
 hot water. Add 3 ml of hydrochloric acid ( HCl, sp gr 1.19 ), cool, and dilute 
 to 100 ml with water. This solution is stable for several months. The pink 
 color that develops slowly does not affect its usefulness.

Note 1: Caution- Brucine 
 sulfate is very toxic; take care to avoid ingestion.
Potassium Nitrate, Standard Solution

(1 ml = 1 mg NO3)-Dry potassium nitrate (KNO3) 
in an oven at105C for 24 h. Dissolve 1.6306 gm in 20 ml of water and dilute to 1 
liter.
Sodium Arsenite Solution ( 1.83 g / liter )

Note 2: Caution- Toxic: take care to avoid 
ingestion.
Sulfuric Acid ( 500+ 75 )

Carefully add 500 ml of sulfuric acid ( H2SO4, sp 
gr 1.84 ) to 75 ml of water. Cool and keep in a tightly stoppered container to 
prevent absorption of moisture.
Sampling

Collect the sample 
 in accordance with the applicable ASTM method, as follows: Sampling Water and 
 Steam, and 
 D3370- Practices for Sampling Water.

Work to be carried 
out
Calibration and Standardization

Prepare a blank and a series of standards using the 
standards nitrate solution. The standards should cover the range 
from 0 to 50 mg/liter of nitrate as No3.
Treat in accordance with procedure from 3 to 9.

Plot the absorbance versus the nitrate 
concentration in mg / liter.

Prepare a calibration curve with each batch of 
samples analyzed.

sections.text: Procedure

If residual 
chlorine is present, add 0.1 ml of arsenite solution to a 50-ml portion of 
sample for each 0.05 mg/liter of chlorine. Add 1 drop in excess and mix.

If the water is 
turbid or has high organic matter ( color ), remove by adding 0.5 g of the 
specially treated activated carbon and 3 ml of aluminum hydroxide cream to 150 
ml of the sample. Mix well, allow to stand for a few minutes and filter, 
discarding the first portion of the filtrate.

Into a clean 
dry 50-ml beaker, pipet a 5.0-ml portion of the filtrate from the previous step or of the 
clear, colorless water containing not more than 50 mg/ liter of nitrate ion.

Add 1.0 ml of 
brucine-sulfanilic acid reagent.

Into a second 
50-ml beaker measure 10 ml of H2SO4.

Mix the 
contents of the two beakers by carefully adding the sample with the 
brucine-sulfanilic acid reagent to the beaker containing the acid. Pour from one 
beaker to the other 6 times to ensure mixing.

Set aside for 
10 1 min in a dark place.

While the color 
is developing add 10 ml of water to the empty 50-ml beaker . After 10 min 
interval, add the 10 ml of water to the sample and mix as before. Allow to cool 
20 to 30 min in the dark.

Measure the 
absorbance of the treated sample at 410 nm against a blank treated similarly to 
the sample except for omitting the addition of the brucine-sulfanilic acid 
reagent.

Determine the 
concentration of NO3 in the sample from a newly prepared calibration curve, 
correcting the observed value for any sample dilution.
